goal: Reproduce project_plan.md section 11.1's plant/controller-model mismatch failure pattern with real Gazebo physics: link2 mass changed in the xacro, controller's linear model NOT regenerated.

verification_run.notable: run 3/3 was not just a threshold miss: stable=false, overshoot_q1_deg=223.7, overshoot_q2_deg=83.7, both actuators saturated at their torque limits (60.0/30.0 Nm) -- a qualitatively different, more severe failure than a borderline settling-time miss.

control_comparison.note: A same-session matched-plant (m1=m2=L1=L2=1.0, no mismatch) LQR/nominal_balance N=3 control was also run (see BENCH-... evidence / HARNESS-001 result.json) and ALSO failed 0/3 -- but with no catastrophic instability in any run (max torque ~22/9 Nm, no saturation). This isolates the mismatch's real effect: it doesn't cause 'more failures' by the pass/fail threshold (both are already 0/3 due to a separate, pre-existing settling-time issue -- see CTRL-003), but it does introduce a distinct, more severe failure mode (torque saturation + real instability) not seen in the matched control.

notes: This is a deliberate, controlled failure used as evidence for HARNESS-001's failure store -- not a bug in this task. The plant/model mismatch is real and physically meaningful (see control_comparison), which is the point: it's genuine evidence for the 'plant-model-inconsistency' skill category, not a fabricated scenario.
